title: SAETA 232
summary: A SAETA Vickers Viscount carrying 55 passengers and four crew members departed Quito for Cuenca on 15 August 1976. The pilot's last contact occurred over Ambato during cruise at high altitude. The aircraft crashed on Chimborazo volcano at 5,310 meters, where the wreckage remained hidden below the glacier for 27 years. No formal investigation was conducted. The cause remains unknown.
probable_cause: The cause of the accident is not known. No investigation was conducted as the accident site was declared a graveyard.

factors.evidence: the pilot's last contact with the control tower took place over the city of Ambato, and the aircraft subsequently crashed on Chimborazo volcano

events.text: On 15 August 1976, a Vickers Viscount departed from Quito bound for Cuenca with 55 passengers and 4 crew

title: 1976 Zagreb mid-air collision

aircraft.type: Hawker Siddeley Trident and Douglas DC-9-32

summary: British Airways Flight 476 (Hawker Siddeley Trident) and Inex-Adria Flight 550 (Douglas DC-9) collided mid-air near Zagreb VOR. The middle-sector controller requested upper-sector controller approval for the DC-9 to climb to flight level 350. The upper-sector controller approved the climb, believing he was watching the correct target climb past an aircraft descending through the same area. Both aircraft were at the same altitude at the collision point. The accident resulted from a procedural error by air traffic controllers in Zagreb.
probable_cause: A procedural error by air traffic controllers in Zagreb, specifically the failure of the upper-sector controller to prevent the climb clearance when an aircraft was descending through the requested flight level.

title: Turkish Airlines 452
summary: Turkish Airlines Flight 452 crashed into Karatepe Hill near Isparta after the first officer mistook city lights of Isparta for the runway at Antalya. The pilots attempted visual flight at night instead of using instruments, mistaking dark mountains for the Mediterranean Sea. The aircraft descended too early and crashed into a hill.
probable_cause: Pilot error: the first officer mistook the city lights of Isparta for the runway of Antalya and the aircraft descended too early. The pilots attempted visual flight instead of required instrumental flight at night.

factors.evidence: The pilots mistook the city lights of Isparta for those of Antalya and the dark area ahead for the Mediterranean Sea.
The pilots were trying to fly visually, instead of instrumental flight, which was required at night.
First Officer Soğangöz responded to the controller's warning: 'Should I believe you, or my eyes?'.
The accident occurred at night when external visual references were degraded.
The aircraft crashed its right wing in a hill at Karatepe and bounced off to the other side of the valley and disintegrated.

events.text: The pilots reported that they could see the lights of the city, while the plane was around 100 km north of it.
When the pilots confirmed they had the runway in sight, the controller at Antalya notified them that he couldn't see them.
Captain Topçuoğlu, who was in the passenger cabin, returned to the cockpit after realizing that something was wrong at an altitude of 150 m.
The aircraft crashed its right wing in a hill, bounced off to the other side of the valley and disintegrated at Karatepe.

title: Cubana 455
summary: Eleven minutes after takeoff from Barbados at 18,000 feet, two bombs detonated on board planted by Cuban exile terrorist group CORU. One bomb in the rear lavatory destroyed control cables, while another in the passenger cabin created a hole and started a fire. The aircraft entered a rapid uncontrolled descent and crashed 8 km offshore. All 73 on board died, including all 24 members of the Cuban national fencing team.
probable_cause: Two time bombs planted by the Coordination of United Revolutionary Organizations, of which anti-Castro Cuban exile groups were responsible.

title: Indian Airlines 171
summary: Indian Airlines Flight 171 suffered an uncontained engine failure of the No. 2 engine shortly after takeoff from Bombay Airport. Metal fatigue in the 10th stage high-pressure compressor disk caused it to disintegrate, with fragments severing fuel lines. Fuel leaked into the engine and ignited, producing an uncontrolled fire that consumed the aircraft's hydraulic fluid. The crew attempted an emergency landing but the aircraft lost control at 300 feet altitude and crashed 1000 yards from the runway end.
probable_cause: Metal fatigue in the 10th stage compressor disk caused an uncontained engine failure with resulting loss of hydraulic fluid due to fire in the engine bay. The crew was unable to recover control of the aircraft and it crashed during the emergency landing approach.

title: 1976 Lloyd Aéreo Boliviano Boeing 707 crash

location.name: El Trompillo Airport, Santa Cruz de la Sierra

summary: The Boeing 707 cargo aircraft struggled to get airborne and crashed shortly after takeoff from El Trompillo Airport. According to eyewitness accounts, an explosion and fire occurred in a left engine before the crash. The aircraft struck a school and stadium, with at least half of the 91 fatalities being children.
probable_cause: Improper flight preparation due to pilot fatigue was the main cause. Engine failure during takeoff meant the aircraft had insufficient thrust to stay airborne.

factors.evidence: It was determined that improper flight preparation due to pilot fatigue was the main cause of the accident
